H plan or P plan: what are you comparing?

A practical starting point for Hong Kong homebuyers and mortgage holders.

Compare the formula, then the payment

An H plan normally links to a specified HIBOR fixing plus a spread, with a cap linked to that bank’s prime rate. A P plan links directly to the bank’s prime rate plus or minus a margin. Each bank may use a different prime rate. A larger discount alone does not tell you which offer is cheaper.

For a simple illustration, suppose HIBOR is 2%, the H spread is 1.3 percentage points, the bank’s prime rate is 5.5%, and the cap is P minus 2 percentage points. The H calculation gives 3.3% and the cap is 3.5%, so the applicable rate in that illustration is 3.3%. If HIBOR rises to 3%, the cap limits it to 3.5%, provided prime stays unchanged. These figures are examples, not market quotations.

A cap can move too

A prime-linked cap is not a fixed rate. When prime changes, the cap can change. Check the fixing period, reset date, rounding convention and the wording in your offer letter. Our calculator uses one constant rate per scenario. It does not forecast HIBOR or prime.

Ask both banks for comparable quotes

  • Use the same property valuation, loan amount and repayment term.
  • Record the reference rate and its date, spread and cap formula.
  • Check legal fees, cashback, lock-in period and redemption penalties.
  • Confirm mortgage insurance eligibility and how its premium is paid.

Try a payment comparison

Enter each quoted effective rate as scenario A or B. The comparison isolates the payment difference at a common loan amount and term. It does not rank the full offers after fees. Use the refinancing view to examine switching costs, and request a bank repayment schedule before committing.
